objective: At the owner's request ('Can we do all 3?', option (c) of FOUR-PLACE-20261031-001's recommendation): do the knot's selected spaces (the non-2-colourable cubic systems) compose into native networks? Using the point lemma and tight-cut factorization (THREEFOLD-AMPLITUDE), determine how the parts of a knot's space meet across cuts: whether a composition can join knot to knot, or must pass through a hub (equality fan-out); what a hub-free failing composition can be; and how the composition reads against the contact-first native-network gate. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-01: the knot's selected spaces compose natively, but only through hubs. Every 3-edge cut of a cubic incidence graph is balanced; across every nontrivial 3-edge cut of a knot's space the line side is exactly the knot (not-all-equal) and the point side exactly a hub (equality), by the point lemma; two sides that both accept knots fail together only as complementary parity cosets, so a hub-free failing composition is a parity one (control: parity does fail hub-free); double cuts of knot's spaces give twelve-class knots that never fail together; the transpose exchanges knot and hub sides. Against the native-network gate this is a native network of knots with network hubs (in scope by the owner's decision), not a hub-free contact network. Recommendation: Continue as approved (the note)
stop_rule: Stop when the interface across every small cut of a knot's space is classified (knot side, hub side, or neither) with proof, the hub-free failing compositions are characterized, and the gate reading is recorded; a hub-free composition of knot's spaces would be recorded as a finding.
title: Composition of the knot's spaces: knots meet through hubs
